correctness.rationale: The matched BB1 recurrence is derived from exact two-coordinate gradient factors; the normalized ratio obeys an exact second-order logarithmic recurrence whose roots have modulus sqrt(2). Component gradient logs are products of those factors. A uniform soft-plus/positive-part bound gives an O(n) log error, a geometric tail gives the universal continuous phase function, and a signed geometric-series identity proves genuine phase variation. The irrational rotation follows from the nonintegral algebraic norm of 1/sqrt(2). The same package includes 252 exact rational factor/ratio checks and 50 finite numerical profile/phase checks; finite tests are only corroborative. The proof covers both balanced and nonbalanced cases and all stated L, ell and gradient signs.

value.rationale: The exact decay law is a natural quantitative refinement of the known two-dimensional superlinear BB1 phenomenon: it resolves the exponential-of-sqrt(2)^n scale, initial imbalance dependence, an eigenvalue-independent universal phase, and persistent extremal oscillations missed by root-rate theory. This is a complete structural asymptotic classification for the minimal genuinely nonlinear BB1 spectral dynamics, with direct interpretation for comparing error thresholds and observed iteration-to-iteration convergence. It does not claim a general algorithmic improvement or a new broad convergence theorem.
